primary_metric: Zero-eligible-day one-contract daily net Sharpe at 0.5 tick/side plus fees vs the 1m close-confirmed continuous stop, decomposed into resolution / wick-trigger / latency
result_summary: Execution-realism investigation of EXP-0009, corrected after a reviewer question. The 1m continuous stop is CLOSE-CONFIRMED (engine.py:158 close<stop, next-1m-open fill); the EXP-0009 1s engine is FIRST-TOUCH (resting stop on sec_low<=stop). These are different exit RULES, not one rule at two resolutions. Decomposition (0.5 tick/side): (1) RESOLUTION is neutral -- a 1s CLOSE-CONFIRMED stop (new trigger=1) reproduces the 1m result exactly, 4209 trades, daily Sharpe 0.9235 vs 0.9226 (+0.0009); (2) the WICK/trigger switch to first-touch is the real effect -- +504 stop exits / +454 trades, -0.447 gross pt/trade, -0.041 daily Sharpe (~478 gross pts, ~1 NQ pt per wick-out), because close-confirmation filters 1m wicks the resting stop takes; (3) LATENCY on the touch model is a further separate -0.115 daily Sharpe / -0.33 gross pt per second. Conclusion: granularity does NOT degrade the strategy; close-confirmation is a beneficial wick filter and the deployed exit is realistic if you wait for the bar close. First-touch (resting stop) is a different, mildly worse policy dominated by premature wick-outs, not latency. Retain the 1m close-confirmed continuous stop. No Null C.
